title: Recognising needs and choosing fair terms

captions.physics: Answering requests with both wishes present
captions.energy: Renewing words after recognising a need

meaning: You can renew a shared promise after an important admission and feel its fairness when each person actually participated in choosing the terms.
text: An important admission can turn habitual consent into a fresh personal choice. The Lovers in the physical position of Vishuddha answer a request with regard for each person’s wishes. Judgement in energy supports readiness to hear a recognised need and renew your shared word. Justice in emotions brings a sense of honest terms. A promise can feel calmer when it matches what both people now understand and can accept. The admission’s significance supports more considered consent without replacing the need for it.

For example, someone admits that repeated “We’ll discuss it later” leaves important things without room. You ask which return to the subject is actually achievable. **Fair terms give an admission a real answer.** An understandable time and a way to announce necessary postponement can be agreed. A request gains space without creating permanent immediate availability. Fairness comes from both people naming possibilities beyond a solemn but impossible sign of participation.

The difficulty is measuring honesty by perfect equality across every later occasion. Any delay looks like breaking the admission’s meaning itself. Discussing specifics preserves respect. New words become dependable when a request’s importance can remain beside both people’s actual circumstances, leaving each exchange free to have a different timing and suitable form of response.
